summary: Ian Kishizawa (1865–1955) worked in Buddhist studies. He studied at Saitama University and under Sotan Oka, later teaching Shunryu Suzuki and Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani.

Ian Mabbett (1939–2020) was an Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Oxford until 1963. He served as Professor of Indian and Buddhist Studies at Aichi Bunkyo University (2000) and Reader in History at Monash University (attested 2003).

Ian Reader (b. 1949) specializes in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies, earning his doctorate from the University of Leeds (circa 1978–1983). His posts include Lecturer at the University of Stirling (~1989–1999), Lancaster University (~1999–2006), and Emeritus Professor at the University of Manchester (~2015).

Ibrahim Shah is an archaeologist who earned his PhD from the University of Peshawar (2001–2007) studying under Farid Khan, Taj Ali, and Ihsan Ali. He held posts as Professor and Chairman at the University of Peshawar (2001) and Associate Professor and Chairman at Hazara University.

Ichijo Ogawa (b. 1936) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Otani University (~1955–1959) and later held posts there as shunin (~1968–2004) and as full-time lecturer at Otani University Junior College (attested 1978).

Ichiro Hori (1910–1974) was a religious studies, Buddhist studies, and history scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and under Kunio Yanagita. He taught at Nishogakusha, Kokugakuin, Tohoku, and Seijo universities, and served as professor emeritus at the University of Tokyo (1965–1971).

Ichiro Katayama (b. 1942) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Komazawa and Otani universities under Kogen Mizuno, and served as associate professor (1975) and professor (1985–2013) at Komazawa University.

Ichiro Numata is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. As of 2026, he is attested as a part-time lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Ichisada Miyazaki (1901–1995) was a sinologist and historian. He studied at Kyoto University under Jitsuzo Kuwabara (~1922–1925) and subsequently held an academic post at Kyoto University (~1936–1965).

Ida Vassalini (1891–1953) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. She earned degrees in philology from the University of Padua and philosophy from the University of Milan, where she also held a teaching post.

Ignatij Andreevich Kossovich (1808–1878) was a linguist who studied at Vilnius University (~1826–1830) and Saint Petersburg State University (~1832–1834). He was Professor of Greek at Polotsk Uniate Theological Seminary (1833–1835) and Docent (1870) and Professor of Greek (1872–1878) at the University of Warsaw.
Ignazio Guidi (1844–1935) studied at the Sapienza University of Rome and later served as a professor there from 1876 to 1919.

Ignác Goldziher (1850–1921) specialized in religious studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University under Ármin Vámbéry, Berlin under Emil Rödiger, Leipzig under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer (PhD ~1869–1870), and Leiden, later serving as privatdozent (1872) and professor (1894) at Eötvös Loránd University.

Igor Dmitrievich Serebryakov (1917–1998) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. After studying at Saint Petersburg State University (~1935–1940), he held posts at the Military Institute of Foreign Languages (~1941–1945), Pravda (~1956–1960), and the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1961–1998).

Igor Dmitrievič Serebrjakov (1917–1998) worked in Indology, studying at Saint Petersburg State University under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (~1935–1940). He served as a teacher at the Military Institute of Foreign Languages (1941–1947) and research fellow at the Institute of Oriental Studies (1961).

Igor Mikhailovich Reisner (1898–1958) was a historian and Indologist. He studied at the Special Faculty of the Frunze Military Academy (~1919–1921) and held a post at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1950–1958).

Ihsan Ali (b. 1955) works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Peshawar and UCL Institute of Archaeology under Frank Raymond Allchin, later serving as Professor at Peshawar, Director of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Directorate (~1997–2002), and Vice Chancellor of Hazara University (~2005–2008).

Ikko Arai is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Komazawa University. Arai studied under Shiro Matsumoto, Kazunobu Matsuda, Lambert Schmithausen, Harunaga Isaacson, and Michael Zimmermann.

Ikuhisa Takigawa (b. 1968) specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Waseda University, Takigawa held posts as a part-time lecturer at Waseda University (~2001) and Tokai University (~2001).
Ikuko Tazaki works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. In 2017, Tazaki was attested as a special researcher at Otani University and a collaborative researcher at Kyoto University.
